about: The boxers built from the owner's meshes on 2026-10-01, and what makes each one itself. tools/build_roster.py reads this. 'age' is muscle strength beside a trained adult's and 'speed' is joint speed beside one's (1.0 = the same); strength also follows the square of height. 'style' is how the boxer is paid in training: the keys are listed in envs/boxing.py where they are read.
veterans_about: Matt and Zombie were trained before the roster existed, from rigs read off the skeleton alone. 'build_roster.py --all' derives them from their meshes like everybody else. Zombie's height is the one his first rig had: his file is not in metres.

trump.says: comes forward, big slow shots to the head, little guard

grandma.says: tight guard, stops the punch, answers with quick shots to the body

grandpa.says: stays at the end of his reach, patient, works behind the left hand
grandpa.style_note: 2026-10-02 04:00, after round 3: taken 1.4 -> 1.0 and crowd 0.8 -> 0.5. As first written he stopped punching in two sessions out of three (with Grandma, then with Lil Matt): a boxer charged that much for a punch taken, at a range few opponents can reach, does best by doing nothing.

nick.says: always closing, many light fast punches

lilmatt.says: gets inside and digs to the body with the right hand
lilmatt.style_note: 2026-10-02 04:00, after round 3: press 0.25 added. He has the shortest arms in the roster and was paid nothing for walking in, so against Grandpa, who stands off, he landed 0.01 punches a second all session.
